evidenceKind: supplied hypothetical observations; not measured audio

cases.name: Awkward but distinctive opening
cases.prompt: Improve this DaemonV12 opening without losing its identity.
observations: The first sound is the clear signature hook.
The first beat obscures the pulse and the hook's final gesture does not connect to the groove entrance.
The groove later uses the same timbre, but different phrasing makes the entrance feel pasted in.
acceptance: Reviews the first 1, 3 and 5 seconds as distinct questions.
Diagnoses deliberate gesture, pulse/context and continuity rather than merely confirming hook presence.
Proposes a cheap timing, trim, pickup, answer or context test and compares the full entrance.
failureSignals: Makes the opening louder as the primary fix.
Passes the opening solely because identity exists at second zero.

cases.name: Technically perfect but safe
cases.prompt: V3 is clean, coherent, balanced and complete, but feels too safe. Decide the next step.
observations: There is no obvious technical defect.
The hook and arrangement remain predictable throughout.
V1, V2 and V3 were complete meaningful renders.
acceptance: Invokes a Risk Pass and proposes exactly one risk tied to the thesis.
States upside, downside, minimum cheap comparison and keep/revert criterion.
Accepts reverting a failed test; does not assume strange means better.
failureSignals: Polishes gain or metrics indefinitely.
Bundles unrelated risks or forces a risky change despite stronger musical evidence for the original.

cases.name: Louder but smaller payoff
cases.prompt: The DaemonV12 payoff measures louder but feels smaller. Diagnose and propose a revision.
observations: Supplied section measurements show higher payoff loudness than the establishment section.
Payoff attacks are softened, stereo contrast decreases and useful pitch range contracts.
The arrangement adds sustained low-mid layers and repeats the hook unchanged.
acceptance: Uses the Impact Test across low end, transients, register, presence, top end, stereo, density, space and musical consequence.
Relates the observed changes to scale and proposes a focused supported arrangement test.
Treats the supplied values as proxy evidence and preserves style-appropriate sparse arrivals.
failureSignals: Uses master gain as the main remedy.
Treats higher loudness as proof of stronger impact.

cases.name: Over-analysis loop
cases.prompt: At V4, I want to write another analyzer to resolve a tiny spectral uncertainty. Decide whether to do it.
observations: V3 and V4 made only marginal improvements.
Existing native analysis and section comparisons are available.
No specific audible decision currently depends on the extra number.
acceptance: Applies musical hypothesis, minimum evidence, cost and keep/revert requirements.
Declines unnecessary new tooling because no unresolved musical decision depends on it.
Compares the stronger existing candidate and stops if final checks pass; leaves room for a genuine material concern or user override.
failureSignals: Builds software just to obtain more metrics.
Uses the five-version default as an absolute engine limit.

cases.name: Low-mid buildup
cases.prompt: A DaemonV12 section feels boxy and loses punch. Several parts overlap roughly 120–500 Hz. Plan the next test.
observations: Bass calls, a pad, distorted source material and long tails overlap.
Some low-mid body serves the musical thesis.
No conventional EQ control has been established in the current engine.
acceptance: Examines overlapping roles, register, source length and tails before broad processing.
Retains useful warmth/body and proposes a focused subtraction, spacing or verified filtering test.
Checks engine support before recommending effects.
failureSignals: Treats 120–500 Hz as universally undesirable.
Invents an EQ control or removes all low-mid energy.

cases.name: Width from arrangement
cases.prompt: Panning a mono sound in this DaemonV12 payoff did not create the width I expected. Explain and propose a supported test.
observations: The source is mono and is duplicated equally into both render channels before pan.
The payoff shifts the same source left and right without adding differing content.
Current-engine pan semantics must be verified from source/spec.
acceptance: Verifies balance/pan semantics and distinguishes positioning from decorrelated content.
Proposes differing answers, timing, octave/timbral doubles or section contrast using supported controls.
Uses stereo and mono comparisons as evidence and acknowledges phase risks.
failureSignals: Claims panning alone generates new decorrelated stereo information.
Chases maximum side energy as a quality target.

cases.name: Interesting ending damages replay
cases.prompt: The DaemonV12 ending is technically clever, but returning to the start feels awkward. Compare alternatives.
observations: The last three seconds introduce an unrelated texture with a long tail.
The opening's deliberate gesture is lost when played after that tail.
The ending is technically valid and unclipped.
acceptance: Reviews final three seconds and end-to-start continuity.
Compares at least two thesis-related replay alternatives and a deliberate version of the existing gesture if useful.
Chooses from musical consequence rather than effect novelty; does not ban the technique.
failureSignals: Keeps the effect just because it is technically interesting.
Mistakes a valid file ending for a replayable composition.

cases.name: Correct decision is stop
cases.prompt: V4 is strong. The proposed V5 has no clear audible hypothesis. Should I render again or lock?
observations: Thesis, intentional opening, readable hook, groove, consequential payoff and replay ending pass review.
No obvious technical defect remains; the Risk Pass was tested and reverted on musical evidence.
Two recent revisions were marginal and remaining ideas are speculative.
acceptance: Locks the stronger V4 rather than inventing a V5 task.
Records stop decision, uncertainty and deterministic lock evidence.
Distinguishes the default iteration budget from user overrides or a genuine new defect.
failureSignals: Runs V5 merely to fill the available version count.
Builds another analyzer without a decision it could change.

cases.name: Hook diversity
cases.prompt: Compose a new DaemonV12 cue. Choose a hook before building the full piece.
observations: Four-bar sketches can use the same verified palette and minimal accompaniment.
There is no human listening feedback yet.
acceptance: Saves 3–4 short hook projects before full V1, with different rhythmic identities and contours; explains the differences.
Validates before cheap dry renders and defers full effects/stems; sketches do not count as V1–V3.
Makes a provisional score-based choice, records uncertainty, and preserves its anchor; uses human selection if feedback arrives.
failureSignals: Offers transpositions or timbre swaps of the same rhythm/contour as different hooks.
Builds four full productions or invents listening and quality scores.

cases.name: Boring repetition
cases.prompt: Develop this repetitive DaemonV12 cue while keeping its recognizable identity.
observations: The two-bar hook is memorable according to supplied human feedback.
The same bass and accompaniment pattern repeats unchanged for 28 seconds.
All events validate and the master is unclipped.
acceptance: Retains the defining hook rhythm/contour and identifies what repeats without consequence.
Plans a focused response, rest, harmonic movement or bass-pattern change; compares a short affected transition before a full render.
Uses subtraction/context to develop the return rather than equating more events with improvement.
failureSignals: Replaces the successful hook by default.
Adds random fills/layers everywhere or treats clean measurements as proof the cue works.

cases.name: Kick/bass ownership
cases.prompt: Plan a cheap repair of this V12 Signature low-end conflict.
observations: The installed pack is 1.0.0 with the verified catalog.
ABYSS holds two overlapping pitches while full-range REACTOR and long SUB HAMMER tails play.
Kick and bass are separate tracks sharing the chokeGroup name bass.
acceptance: Assigns one sub owner per moment, removes conflicting sub pitches and checks gate plus release and effect tails.
Uses a focused spacing/gating or authored gain-ramp test; considers REACTOR highpass at 110 Hz over ABYSS.
Explains track-local chokes cannot solve cross-track collisions and root phase alignment does not prevent overload or guarantee repitched alignment.
failureSignals: Adds bass, invokes automatic sidechain, or assumes a shared group guarantees cross-track monophony.
Claims score inspection alone proves the repair sounds better.

cases.name: Weak drop from full setup
cases.prompt: The V12 Signature drop measures louder but has no impact. Propose one arrangement test.
observations: The build already contains every role at full density, including held sub, kick and lead.
The drop repeats the same bass pattern and hook register with an added impact.
Supplied human feedback calls the hook strong and the arrival weak.
acceptance: Preserves the hook and tests a lighter setup through subtraction, a harmonic hold or an early stop.
Changes the arrival bass pattern or register/context so the return has a consequence; compares approach and arrival together.
Labels measured loudness as technical evidence, uses listening when available, and keeps the change provisional without it.
failureSignals: Raises master gain, adds every remaining instrument, or assigns an automatic drop-quality score.
Rewrites the hook instead of testing the setup/arrival relationship.

cases.name: Preserve hook through revision
cases.prompt: V2 needs less masking. Revise it without losing the strong hook.
observations: The saved winning sketch has a distinctive displaced rhythm and rising leap with a falling answer.
Supplied human feedback prefers that hook and V1 groove.
V2 added sustained chords over the lead; a proposed V3 replaces the melody, rhythm, drums and harmony at once.
acceptance: Names keep/change/evidence needed and protects the saved rhythm/contour and successful groove.
Tests only the implicated chord voicing/tails/placement or subtraction, compares to the anchor and full transition, and reverts lost identity.
Requires an explicit hypothesis or user request for replacing the hook; stops speculative iteration after two marginal revisions while completing final review/Risk Pass.
failureSignals: Accepts the blanket rewrite as normal revision.
Declares a new hook superior from peak, event count or clean validation without listening evidence.

cases.name: Portable workflow without Signature
cases.prompt: Use Composer for a sparse acoustic DaemonV12 cue; V12 Signature is unavailable.
observations: Only the engine and a copied Composer skill directory are available; no Signature catalog or WAVs exist.
The brief calls for acoustic call-and-response and a quiet harmonic arrival.
acceptance: Loads packaged hook-first guidance and uses available verified instruments without requiring Signature or downloading assets.
Compares short rhythmic/contour alternatives appropriate to acoustic pacing, including deliberate low-end absence.
Keeps normal critique and Risk Pass; does not force A minor, electronic drums or a drop.
failureSignals: Fails because repository playbook is missing or silently assumes Signature is installed.
Invents Signature paths or forces the electronic showcase recipe.
